OPS_001.context: Before earthworks started, a cable line was found that is not on the utilities drawing.
OPS_001.text: How will you check the conditions for authorising excavation?

options.A: I will compare the as-built drawings with the actual utility positions together with the utility owner.
options.B: I will suspend the excavation and formalise a change to the work permit.
options.C: I will clarify the position of the line, then update the permit and the work boundaries.
options.D: I will fence off the spot and pass the discrepancy to the person responsible for permits.

OPS_002.context: A section of guardrail is missing on the scaffolding, and the contractor is waiting for permission to work.
OPS_002.text: How will you respond to the request to start the shift?

options.A: I will close access and organise restoration and inspection of the scaffolding with the team.
options.B: I will tell the contractor clearly that access is closed until the guardrail is restored.
options.C: I will mark the danger zone and inform the responsible manager.
options.D: I will gather the supervisor and the installers to agree restoration and a repeat inspection.

OPS_003.context: While a load was being lifted, a small object fell next to a walkway; no one was hurt.
OPS_003.text: How will you investigate the incident?

options.A: I will raise the issue at the operational meeting and propose immediate measures.
options.B: I will file an incident report and pass it to the commission.
options.C: I will reconstruct the lifting sequence and check how the load was secured and the route.
options.D: I will record the facts, flag the risk to the manager and secure measures before the next lift.

OPS_004.context: A subcontractor's permit for work at height has expired, although the crew is included in the daily plan.
OPS_004.text: How will you organise the day?

options.A: I will inform the planner of the restriction and record a new date for the work.
options.B: I will check the documents and, together with the site manager, move the crew to permitted work.
options.C: I will agree safe tasks on the ground with the crew until the permit is issued.
options.D: I will not allow work at height and will follow up on restoring the permit.

OPS_005.context: Remarks about helmets keep recurring on the section, although there are spare helmets in the warehouse.
OPS_005.text: How will you look for a lasting solution?

options.A: I will check helmet sizes, how helmets are issued and the circumstances of each repeat case.
options.B: I will discuss with the workers what prevents them from wearing helmets and collect suggestions.
options.C: I will compare the reasons for the remarks with the crew's opinion and change the issue procedure or the control.
options.D: I will check the issue log and schedule a repeat safety briefing.

OPS_006.context: A new worker is not sure that the electrical panel is switched off, and installation is already scheduled.
OPS_006.text: How will you ensure a safe start?

options.A: I will secure the electrician's confirmation and a permit before installation starts.
options.B: I will openly stop the preparation and call an authorised electrician to check.
options.C: I will fence off the area and send the worker to the person responsible for electrical installations.
options.D: I will check that the work permit has been issued and electrical isolation confirmed according to the procedure.

OPS_007.context: The delivery route crosses the tower crane's working zone.
OPS_007.text: How will you coordinate vehicle movements?

options.A: I will record the approved route and the restrictions in the traffic plan.
options.B: I will suspend entry and request a decision from the person responsible for lifting.
options.C: I will check the lifting plan, the delivery schedule and possible detour routes.
options.D: I will find a safe route and enter it into the agreed traffic plan.

OPS_008.context: The subcontractor's safety briefing describes different operations from the actual installation on the floor.
OPS_008.text: How will you handle authorisation for the crew to work?

options.A: I will request a corrected briefing and schedule a repeat check.
options.B: I will not allow the crew to work until the corrected safety briefing has been given; we will discuss it with the workers.
options.C: Together with the supervisor and the crew, I will clarify the operations and the measures needed.
options.D: I will firmly refuse authorisation to work and explain the mismatch to the works manager.

OPS_009.context: During roof work, wind readings at ground level and at the top differ noticeably.
OPS_009.text: How will you decide whether to continue lifting materials?

options.A: I will check the measuring location and that the instrument works, then compare the values with the limits.
options.B: I will tell the manager that a pause is needed until there is a reliable measurement.
options.C: I will stop lifting, get a repeat measurement at the top and record the decision.
options.D: I will request a control measurement from the responsible person and keep the load on the ground.

OPS_010.context: A worker reported pain after carrying materials by hand and wants to finish the shift.

options.A: I will provide help, register the report and hand the task over to another worker.
options.B: I will arrange for medical help and file the report according to the procedure.
options.C: I will notify the supervisor and send the worker to a medical specialist.
options.D: I will coordinate a replacement in the crew and help the worker leave the site safely.

OPS_011.context: The supplier changed the safety data sheet for the sealant that the crew uses every day.
OPS_011.text: How will you introduce the updated requirements?

options.A: I will discuss the changes with the crew and collect questions about its use.
options.B: I will pass the new data sheet to the supervisor and arrange for workers to read it.
options.C: I will compare the composition, risks and ventilation requirements with the previous data sheet.
options.D: I will check the differences in the data sheet and adjust the work procedure together with the workers.

OPS_012.context: The manager asks you to temporarily open a passage across the site without an approved access plan.
OPS_012.text: How will you respond to the request?

options.A: I will fence off the route and pass the request to the person responsible for site layout.
options.B: I will keep the passage closed and initiate approval of a temporary route.
options.C: I will request a plan, an inspection and a permit under the current procedure.
options.D: I will explain why the passage is closed for now and propose a safe alternative.

OPS_013.context: Before entering a manhole it turned out that the gas detector calibration log is not fully filled in.
OPS_013.text: How will you check readiness for the work?

options.A: I will check the serial number, the valid metrological verification and the results of the instrument's control check.
options.B: I will not allow entry and will restore the documents and atmosphere testing according to the procedure.
options.C: I will check the instrument, record the data and issue a permit only after the air has been tested.
options.D: I will close the entry and call the person responsible for the gas detector.

OPS_014.context: The contractor asks to remove part of the guardrail at an opening to carry equipment through.
OPS_014.text: How will you organise the operation?

options.A: I will set the conditions for temporary access and make sure the crew restores the protection.
options.B: I will firmly demand a temporary solution that keeps fall protection in place.
options.C: I will pass the request to the supervisor and schedule an inspection of the area before the operation.
options.D: I will agree with the installers the order of carrying the equipment and restoring the guardrail.

OPS_015.context: Two shifts mark the same danger zone near the warehouse differently.
OPS_015.text: How will you resolve the inconsistency?

options.A: I will raise the issue with the shift managers and point out the need for a single scheme.
options.B: I will keep the wider fencing until a common decision is made.
options.C: I will compare the actual movement paths, the scheme and the reasons for the different markings.
options.D: I will check the risk and secure a single agreed marking for both shifts.

OPS_016.context: The hot work permit expires before the actual end of welding.

options.A: I will remind the supervisor of the deadline and prepare a new permit in advance.
options.B: I will finish work within the permit's validity period, then agree the new shift and protective measures.
options.C: I will agree with the crew to postpone the remaining welds and arrange a fire watch.
options.D: I will stop welding by the deadline and formalise an extension with a repeat check of the area.

OPS_017.context: Several workers bypass the designated pedestrian route to take a shortcut to the site cabin.
OPS_017.text: How will you find the cause and change the behaviour?

options.A: I will check the length of the route, the lighting and the actual points where it crosses vehicle paths.
options.B: I will discuss with the workers the obstacles on the route and ways to improve it.
options.C: I will check the risk of the crossings and, together with the team, propose a convenient safe route.
options.D: I will strengthen the route signage and hold a targeted briefing.

OPS_018.context: The supervisor disputes a remark about cylinders placed next to the welding area.
OPS_018.text: How will you resolve the situation?

options.A: I will explain the requirement, record the moving of the cylinders and check the result.
options.B: I will firmly show the specific requirement and stop the use of the cylinders until it is corrected.
options.C: I will pass the remark to the person responsible for welding and set a date for checking.
options.D: I will check the placement and record a remark with a follow-up inspection.

OPS_019.context: After the rain, the walkway near the excavation was washed out, but earthworks have not yet resumed.
OPS_019.text: How will you assess the readiness of the section?

options.A: I will close the walkway and update the access scheme before re-admission.
options.B: I will inform the site manager and keep the walkway closed until it is checked.
options.C: I will inspect the stability of the slope, the drainage and the condition of the route with the responsible specialist.
options.D: I will assess the condition of the excavation, update the fencing and arrange a repeat inspection.

OPS_020.context: The foreman reports that the workers do not understand the new evacuation procedure from two levels.
OPS_020.text: How will you carry out the preparation?

options.A: I will pass the clarified scheme to the supervisors and set a time for the briefing.
options.B: I will get the scheme explained and hold a joint drill before work starts.
options.C: I will organise a practical walk-through of the routes with both crews and collect questions.
options.D: I will tell the managers that admission is impossible without a clear evacuation procedure.

OPS_021.context: Conflicting reports came in on site about damage to a temporary cable.
OPS_021.text: How will you find out the extent of the risk?

options.A: I will clarify the location, load and condition of the cable with the electrician and from the inspection log.
options.B: I will demand that access to the area be closed and inform those responsible of the possible damage.
options.C: I will fence off the area, arrange a check by an electrician and communicate the result to the shift.
options.D: I will pass the information to the duty electrician and keep the fencing in place.

OPS_022.context: The contractor wants to work on a day off, when regular supervision of the site is not planned.
OPS_022.text: How will you organise the approval?

options.A: I will check the availability of duty staff and agree a feasible scope of work with the team.
options.B: I will check the duty roster, the permit and the responsible people before confirming the work.
options.C: I will reschedule unprepared work and notify everyone on the schedule.
options.D: I will connect the contractor with the duty services and agree a feasible safe task.

OPS_023.context: Workers have complained about dust in the tile cutting area.
OPS_023.text: How will you choose the measures?

options.A: I will collect the workers' suggestions on equipment placement and protection.
options.B: I will pass the complaints to the supervisor and arrange measurement of the conditions if needed.
options.C: I will check the source, the cutting mode and how the dust extraction actually works.
options.D: I will check the causes of the dust and, together with the crew, change the cutting method and control.

OPS_024.context: The contractor asks you to accept verbal authorisation to enter a restricted technical area.

options.A: I will provide the contact details of the person responsible for the area and keep the entrance closed.
options.B: I will keep the restriction and help arrange an official permit.
options.C: I will check the list of authorised persons and arrange access according to the established procedure.
options.D: I will firmly explain that entry is impossible without a confirmed permit.

OPS_025.context: The rebar order specifies a diameter from an old design revision, and shipment is scheduled for the morning.
OPS_025.text: How will you clarify the order?

options.A: I will check the design revision, the materials list and the confirmed quantities with the technical department (PTO) engineer.
options.B: I will freeze the shipment and file a corrected order according to the procedure.
options.C: I will confirm the current diameter and update the order before the shipment is approved.
options.D: I will report the discrepancy to the person who placed the order and wait for confirmation.

OPS_026.context: Concrete blocks and equipment for urgent installation arrived at the unloading area at the same time.
OPS_026.text: How will you allocate the ramp resources?

options.A: I will set the priority and agree the time for each unloading with the participants.
options.B: I will tell the drivers the unloading order and agree it with the warehouse manager.
options.C: I will register both vehicles and request a decision on the order from the dispatcher.
options.D: I will bring together the warehouse representative, the site manager and the drivers to agree safe time slots.

OPS_027.context: The supplier offers a cheaper equivalent cable, but its fire resistance is unclear in the data sheet.
OPS_027.text: How will you assess the offer?

options.A: I will openly refuse to approve the substitution without confirmation of the parameters.
options.B: I will send the data sheet to the designer and keep the original item in the order.
options.C: I will compare the required marking and certificates with the design specification.
options.D: I will check the documents and explain to the supplier what data is needed for consideration.

OPS_028.context: A batch of fasteners arrived before the installation area was ready and is blocking the warehouse aisle.

options.A: I will temporarily allocate a free permitted spot and inform the warehouse.
options.B: I will formalise the move and discuss the earliest issue date with the crew.
options.C: I will agree with the storekeeper and the installers on placement that does not block the aisle.
options.D: I will determine a permissible area and record the move in the warehouse records.

OPS_029.context: Installers often request small fittings on the day of work, which causes downtime.
OPS_029.text: How will you change the supply arrangements?

options.A: I will collect the issue history and identify items with unstable stock.
options.B: I will discuss the weekly need and a convenient request format with the supervisors.
options.C: I will compare consumption with the schedule and set up a minimum stock with the crews.
options.D: I will suggest that the supervisors submit a list of fittings for the week in advance.

OPS_030.context: The site manager asks by phone to send material to another site without a delivery note.

options.A: I will explain the procedure, quickly formalise the transfer and give the delivery time.
options.B: I will clearly confirm that the transfer is possible only after it is formalised.
options.C: I will clarify the site details and start the approval with the person responsible.
options.D: I will prepare the documents and check the stock before sending.

OPS_031.context: The delivery note says 120 bags of mix, but 116 were counted on the pallets during acceptance.
OPS_031.text: How will you carry out the acceptance?

options.A: I will record the discrepancy in a report and adjust the receipt according to the procedure.
options.B: I will leave the delivery note unsigned and call the senior storekeeper.
options.C: I will recount the pallets and check the labelling with the driver.
options.D: I will check the actual quantity and record the discrepancy before signing the acceptance.

OPS_032.context: The supplier warned that delivery of the window units will be three days late.
OPS_032.text: How will you inform the team?

options.A: I will pass the notice to those responsible and request an updated schedule.
options.B: I will openly report the delay and help the team agree interim work.
options.C: I will gather the site manager, the planner and the supplier to agree a new sequence.
options.D: I will name the confirmed date and immediately point out the impact on the schedule.
